latin: Empedocles per litem et amicitiam in anima nihil aliud intelligit quam potentiam sursum ductiuam et deorsum ductiuam in ea, quas ego credo proportionari in scientia sephirot aeternitati et decori.
translation: By strife and friendship in the soul, Empedocles points to nothing more than the upward-drawing and downward-drawing powers within it, which I take to correspond, in the science of the sefirot, to Eternity and Beauty.
translation_note: 'aeternitati et decori' name the seventh and eighth sefirot (Netzach and Hod) in Pico's kabbalistic correspondences.
